about:
![Ear Collector logo: a severed ear in a gold ring](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/main/docs/logo.png)

# Ear Collector

A World of Warcraft addon for **WoW Forever** that collects an ear from every
enemy player you or your group kill in the open world, like the ears PvP kills
dropped in Diablo II.

- Kills by you, your pet, your group and their pets count. So do assists: kills
  someone outside your group finished after you damaged the victim or earned
  honor for them.
- Battlegrounds, arenas and dungeons never count.
- Each ear shows the victim's race and a grade for how hard-won the kill was.
  Ears go in an Ear Pouch, with a Ledger of totals and a list of Rivals.
- Everything stays on your screen. Ear Collector never posts to chat or sends
  anything other players can see.

Ear Collector is heavily AI-authored. See [How it's made](#how-its-made).

## Install

1. Download `EarCollector-<version>-forever.zip` from the
   [releases page](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases).
2. Unzip it into the `Interface/AddOns/` folder of your WoW Forever
   installation, so that you have `Interface/AddOns/EarCollector/EarCollector.toc`.
3. Start the game, or type `/reload`.

To update, delete the `EarCollector` folder and unzip the new one. Your ears are
saved outside it. Each character keeps its own collection, and the settings are
shared by all your characters.

## Use

Open the pouch with `/ears`, your bags, the minimap addon drawer, a key binding
(Key Bindings > AddOns), or by clicking an ear's name in chat. Escape closes it.
The options are in Options > AddOns > Ear Collector.

The small coloured buttons at the top left of the Ears tab hide or show each
grade. Click the grey one to put away your Poor ears; they stay saved and still
count in the Ledger and Rivals.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/ears` | Open or close the pouch |
| `/ears options` | Open the options |
| `/ears stats` | Your totals and latest ear |
| `/ears recent [n]` | Your newest ears (5 unless you give a number) |
| `/ears bags on\|off` | Open the pouch with your bags |
| `/ears popup on\|off` | The pop-up when you collect an ear |
| `/ears popup move` | Drag pop-ups where you want them |
| `/ears popup reset` | Put pop-ups back near the top of the screen |
| `/ears sound on\|off` | The pop-up's sound |
| `/ears debug` | Print and save what the addon sees, for testing and bug reports |
| `/ears errors` | Errors the addon caught (it keeps running) |

### Grades

An ear's grade says how much the kill felt like an achievement, from Poor to
Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic and Legendary. Each of these counts for or against:

- **The odds:** being outnumbered counts for you, outnumbering them counts against.
- **The danger to you:** how much damage you took, in health bars.
- **How strong they were:** their health compared with yours counts for more
  than how long the fight lasted, so a quick burst on a big target is rewarded.
- **How fast they fell:** bringing them down within seconds counts for you,
  unless they were lower than you and smaller, or you had them outnumbered.
- **Whether they fought back:** picking off a smaller, lower player who never
  hit you counts against you.
- **Your part:** your healing and shields, your side's interrupts and dispels,
  and group members who fell.
- **Their level:** every level above you counts for you, and every level below
  against, most of all for orange and red, or green.
- **Revenge:** each time they've killed you since you last killed them. Three
  times makes their next ear Legendary.
- **Repeats:** a second or third ear from the same player in a day counts a
  little less.

The fight is read from the game's damage meter, which addons can only see once
combat ends. So an ear taken in a fight waits quietly, with nothing to distract
you mid-fight, and once combat ends, chat and the pop-up show it graded. With no record
of the fight, the grade follows the victim's level colour. Grey victims, who give
no honor, are Poor unless revenge raises them.

Hover an ear to see why it has its grade: each reason with a + or -, and
squares for how much it counted. When the kill has a story worth telling, a
gold line tells it in your own words: "They had the edge on me. They never had
the time." or "They should have quit while they were ahead."

Killing the same player again within 10 minutes adds to that ear instead of
dropping a new one. The options set the window.

### Rivals

The Rivals tab lists everyone you've taken an ear from or died to. **Avenge**
means they've killed you since you last killed them, so their next ear is worth
more (Legendary after three times). **Nemesis** means they've killed you more
often than you've killed them, and **Prey** means you've killed them three times
or more and they've never killed you.

Ear Collector keeps your grudges. When someone you owe shows up again on a
later day, chat reminds you, and for Vengeance a pop-up and the raid warning
sound do too. Reminders come only out of combat. Someone who killed you an hour ago won't set it off, and neither
will the same player again that day. Hovering anyone you owe shows the grudge
on their tooltip.

### What it can't see

WoW Forever doesn't give addons the combat log, so Ear Collector works from the
game's kill and honor reports and its damage meter.

- An assist counts only when the enemy player dies near you.
- Who killed you comes from the death recap, matched against the enemy players
  you could see or had hit. If none of them matches, the death isn't recorded.

## How it's made

Ear Collector is heavily AI-authored. Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent,
wrote most of the code, the tests, the documentation, and the scripts that paint
the ears and the logo. The maintainer decides what it does and how it looks,
merges every change, and tests it in the game. Every AI-assisted commit carries
an `Assisted-by:` trailer, and [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) has the
rules AI-assisted contributions follow.

## Reporting a bug

Open an [issue](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/issues) and include
what `/ears errors` lists.

## Contributing

See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Ear Collector

## [v2.2.1](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/tree/v2.2.1) (2026-11-28)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/compare/v2.2.0...v2.2.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases)

- fix: grade brawls from the meter's fight, and stay quiet until combat ends (#57)  
    In a brawl that comes and goes (several groups, combat dropping and  
    returning), the meter can keep one session across several of our fights.  
    A kill in a later one then found no session newer than when its fight  
    began, and its ear read "No record of the fight". When a fight's own  
    session can't be told, the meter's current fight now serves, if the  
    victim is among the enemies in it (or the meter hides who everyone is).  
    With /ears debug on, an ear with no record logs why.  
    Nothing about an ear is said in combat any more, so a chaotic fight isn't  
    interrupted: an ear taken in combat waits in silence, however long the  
    fight runs, and gets its "You collected" line and pop-up, graded, when  
    combat ends. The 30-second ungraded pop-up and the "Appraising the  
    fight..." line are gone, and a camped repeat in combat goes unsaid.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

# Ear Collector

## [v2.2.0](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/tree/v2.2.0) (2026-11-27)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/compare/v2.1.0...v2.2.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases)

- feat(ui): drop the "Why it's " line from ear tooltips (#56)  
    The reasons already sit in their own block, with a blank line on either  
    side, right under the grade; the header only repeated the grade.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- fix(grading): find each fight's meter record reliably (#55)  
    A fight took its meter session at the moment combat ended, and only if the  
    newest session had changed since the fight before. When the meter lists a  
    fight's session a moment after combat ends, the fight got none, and its  
    ears read "No record of the fight": the maintainer's Epic assist in Eastern  
    Plaguelands, for one.  
    A fight's session is now the one the meter reports updating  
    (DAMAGE\_METER\_COMBAT\_SESSION\_UPDATED) during it or up to 5 seconds after;  
    failing that, the newest session if it's newer than the newest when the  
    fight began. It's worked out when the fight is read, and settled when the  
    next fight begins, so a new fight still can't lend an old one its session.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

# Ear Collector

## [v2.1.0](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/tree/v2.1.0) (2026-11-25)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/compare/v2.0.1...v2.1.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases)

- feat: count every level and a burst, and tell the kill in your own words (#54)  
    * feat: count every level and a burst, and make the gold line a story  
    Small upsides now count the way small downsides already did, so the tooltip  
    shows the whole picture. Within yellow, each level a victim is above you is  
    +2 (two levels: +4) and each level below is -2, down to -6; orange, red and  
    green are unchanged. A kill within 8 seconds of entering combat is "Down in  
    seconds", +4, except on someone lower than you who didn't have your health,  
    or when you had them outnumbered two to one. Each ear saves the level gap.  
    The gold line now tells the most memorable part of the kill, to be fun: a  
    grudge settled ("Three times they took your ear. Not this time."), or the  
    strongest reasons pointing the same way ("Two levels above you, and gone in  
    seconds."). There's none when there's nothing worth telling, such as a  
    small markdown alone. The list above it still accounts for every point.  
    Tooltip lines for orange, red and green name the level gap.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    * feat(ui): "gone in a moment" in the story  
    The maintainer's wording for a burst in the gold line. The tooltip's list  
    line stays "Down in seconds", which states the rule.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    * feat(ui): tell the kill in the player's own words  
    The gold line becomes the kill as the player would tell it to a friend  
    afterwards: first person, in degrees rather than numbers ("They had me well  
    outnumbered.", "They were well out of my league, and it didn't save them."),  
    with no mention of ears. The list above it keeps every fact.  
    The strongest reason picks the tale, and some pairings have their own: an  
    edge and a burst ("They had the edge on me. They never had the time."),  
    outnumbered and outlevelled, the numbers with no damage taken, a tanky foe  
    and your healing. A death takes over any line that would say you came  
    through it. A grudge settled takes the whole line, by degree of spite: a  
    slight, a grudge or a vendetta, each with a few lines the ear picks between,  
    so the same ear always reads the same and different ears vary. Nothing is  
    told for an even kill, a small markdown or a lower level. Chat quotes the  
    tale after the grade.  
    The tales live in UI/Tales.lua; UI/Reasons.lua is back to the list lines.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    ---------  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

## [v2.0.1](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/tree/v2.0.1) (2026-11-22)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/compare/v2.0.0...v2.0.1) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases)

- fix(grudges): remind you only out of combat (#53)  
    A grudge reminder no longer comes in combat. Seeing someone you owe for the  
    first time that day while you're fighting counts as meeting them, so no  
    reminder follows once the fight ends either; the next one can come on a  
    later day, out of combat. Tooltip lines on hover are unchanged.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- test: record the saved file v2.0.0 writes (#52)

    so its SavedVariables join spec/fixtures/saved, recorded by playing the  
    evening in a v2.0.0 checkout, and every later version is tested against it.  
    Recording it found a bug in spec/support/saved\_evening.lua: a saved band  
    named "repeat", a Lua keyword, was written as a bare key, which doesn't

# Ear Collector

## [v2.0.0](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/tree/v2.0.0) (2026-11-22)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/compare/v1.4.0...v2.0.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/AlexaDeWit/Ear-Collector/releases)

- feat: remember grudges, and remind you when an old one shows up (#51)  
    * feat: remember grudges, and remind you when an old one shows up  
    A player who took your ear since you last took theirs is a grudge. When one  
    shows up (their nameplate, your target or your mouseover, where kills count)  
    and you last fought them on an earlier day and at least 6 hours ago, chat  
    reminds you once that day. Vengeance also shows a red pop-up framed in  
    Legendary and plays the raid warning, which an option can silence. A day of  
    back and forth stays quiet. Hovering anyone you owe adds the grudge to their  
    tooltip, through TooltipDataProcessor and TooltipUtil, both checked in  
    Forever's own source.  
    Deaths.Debt now scans your deaths before your ears, so the common case (a  
    player who never killed you) costs a short loop.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    * feat: word grudge reminders as "You owe them one"  
    The maintainer's pick: the pop-up's label and the tooltip line say "You owe  
    them one", and chat says "You owe Cedric Vale one. They took your ear three  
    times in a row, last on Nov 18. Their next ear is Legendary."  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    ---------  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat(ui): say why an ear has its grade (#50)  
    The ear's tooltip now lists what counted under "Why it's ": each  
    reason on its own line with a + or - and one to three squares for how much  
    it counted, in player terms ("Outnumbered 1v2", "Took more than a full  
    health bar", "Twice your health"). A story of one or two sentences closes  
    the tooltip in gold and follows the grade in chat: "You were outnumbered two  
    to one and took more than a full health bar, but it was your second ear from  
    them in a day." The pop-up's detail line names the strongest reason.  
    Vengeance and grey ears show the rule that set their grade, with the fight  
    in grey as context. Ears with no fight record, no reasons, or a grade still  
    waiting on the fight each say so. The wording is the copy the maintainer  
    ratified; spec/fight\_summary\_spec.lua holds its ten samples.  
    The Hard-fought, Fair fight and One-sided headings are gone: they counted  
    only the fight, so they could contradict a grade that revenge or level set.  
    An assist is now lowered only when the meter gave a damage figure, so "took  
    little damage" is never a guess.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- fix(grading): grade a kill only from its own fight (#49)  
    A kill graded out of combat, such as your group's kill while you weren't  
    fighting, was graded from your last fight on the damage meter, however long  
    ago it ended. It now uses that fight only if it ended within Assists.RECENT,  
    the same window assists use; otherwise the ear is graded by the kill alone.  
    A fight also took the newest meter session when combat ended, which is the  
    previous fight's when the meter kept no record of this one. A fight now has  
    a session of its own only if the newest changed since the last fight ended  
    (or since login), and a fight without one isn't read.  
    The fake meter now rejects a session ID of the wrong type, as the client's  
    own functions do.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat(data): migration steps for saved data, safe in both directions (#48)  
    Saved data now loads through numbered steps (Database.STEPS) that run once  
    each, in order, on a copy that replaces the saved table only if every step  
    finishes. A failed step leaves the player's data exactly as it was, and the  
    steps run again next load. A file saved by a newer version keeps its schema  
    and every field, and the player is told once. Repair now drops only known  
    fields of the wrong type, never fields it doesn't know.  
    Schema 3: every ear keeps how it was graded. New ears save each band's  
    points and the rule (vengeance or grey) from the moment they're recorded, so  
    an ear still reads the same after the bands are retuned. Ears from earlier  
    releases get the record their grade came from: every release so far graded  
    by level colour alone, or Vengeance.  
    spec/fixtures/saved holds SavedVariables written by v1.0.0, v1.4.0 and the  
    test builds before v2.0.0, recorded by playing the same evening in each  
    release (spec/support/saved\_evening.lua), plus a hand-written newer file.  
    The guidance for changing what's saved is in docs/architecture.md, with a  
    rule in CONTRIBUTING.md and a pointer in AGENTS.md.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- feat: grade ears by how hard the kill felt (#47)  
    * feat: grade ears by how hard the kill felt  
    An ear's grade now says how much the kill felt like an achievement, not  
    just the level gap. Each signal falls into a named band worth some  
    points:  
    - the odds, and how much damage you took in health bars  
    - how long the fight lasted, and a fight where they never hit back  
    - the victim's toughness, your healing and shields, interrupts and  
      dispels, allies who fell, and your own death  
    - the level colour  
    - revenge for each death owed, and earlier ears from them that day  
    The total falls into grade buckets that widen as grades rise. Three  
    deaths owed is still Legendary, grey victims are Poor unless revenge  
    raises them, and any other ear is at least Common. A signal the game  
    doesn't give is worth nothing, so without a fight record the grade is  
    the level colour's, as before.  
    The damage meter is secret in combat, so an ear taken in a fight waits:  
    chat says "Appraising the fight...", and when the fight ends the meter  
    is read once, each waiting ear is graded, and its chat line and pop-up  
    follow. Its pop-up shows ungraded if the fight runs 30 seconds past the  
    kill. The facts and the bands that counted are saved on the ear, shown  
    in its tooltip, and logged by /ears debug.  
    Rivals marks "Avenge" from the first death owed, under Nemesis, and  
    death lines and pop-ups say revenge is owed.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo  
    * feat: weigh a strong foe above a long fight  
    A clean burst can end a fight with a much bigger opponent in a couple of  
    global cooldowns, and that should count. The victim's maximum health  
    against yours is now a band: 1.25 times +5, 1.5 times +9, twice +13,  
    however short the fight. Fight length drops to +2 at 30 seconds and +4  
    at 60, and odds of three and two to one rise to +20 and +13, so being  
    alone against three and near death stays Legendary.  
    "They never fought back" now counts against you only when the foe was  
    smaller than you and not a higher level, so a burst on an equal or  
    stronger foe isn't marked down as a gank.  
    Assisted-by: Claude Code (Anthropic)  
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session\_015r8sLrFyydpRPQPGKHAkKo
